source: ONS Living Costs and Food Survey (LCF) via Family Spending workbook 1: detailed expenditure and trends, FYE 2024
notes: TIER A (UK): REAL primary-source data from ONS's Living Costs and Food Survey (LCF), published in the 'Family Spending' report series, UK financial year ending (FYE) 2024 (April 2023-March 2024), n=4,210 sampled households, weighted to 28.48 million UK households. All £ figures converted from the source's native 'average weekly household expenditure/income' units to ANNUAL figures via x52.1786 (365.25/7 weeks/year) for consistency with the annual-figure convention used elsewhere in this v2 dataset (e.g. BLS CES); values remain in nominal GBP (local currency) per the task instruction that non-USD currency data stay in local currency for the frontend to convert via PPP at display time. DECILE BASIS CAVEAT: this file's 'rows' groups are DISPOSABLE-income deciles (Table 3.1), which is the closest LCF equivalent to BLS CES's after-tax income concept, but the boundaries differ from the GROSS-income deciles used for 'avg_income_before_tax' (Table A6, mean gross income by GROSS-income decile group) -- ONS explicitly disaggregates by gross-income decile and disposable-income decile SEPARATELY and does not publish a single table with both income concepts cut by the same decile boundary. avg_income_before_tax values are therefore the gross-income-decile mean paired positionally (1st with 1st, 2nd with 2nd, etc.) with the disposable-income-decile's expenditure figures -- a reasonable but imperfect proxy since decile membership can differ slightly between the two income concepts; flagged here rather than fabricating a joint distribution. CATEGORY MAPPING (source COICOP-based headings -> v2 schema): housing = ONS row '4 Housing (net), fuel & power' [excludes mortgage interest/capital repayments/council tax by ONS convention] PLUS row '13.1 Housing: mortgage interest payments, council tax etc.' (combined to give a housing measure closer to CES's all-in housing bucket, though CES imputes owners' rent while LCF's 'net' housing concept generally does NOT include imputed rental value for owner-occupiers -- see housing_owner_imputed_rent_estimate=null caveat below). food_at_home = row 1.1 'Food' (excludes row 1.2 non-alcoholic drinks, which per COICOP is technically food-adjacent but reported separately by ONS; not re-added to avoid ambiguity, folded into 'other'). food_away = row 11.1 'Catering services' (restaurant/cafe meals, alcohol away from home, takeaway, canteens) -- ONS bundles some alcohol-away-from-home into this row, a minor definitional mismatch vs a pure food-away measure. healthcare_oop = row 6 'Health' -- SUPPRESSED (shown as '..') at the decile level in the published table for statistical disclosure/small-sample reasons; only the 'All households' aggregate (£7.60/week) is published. Set to null for all deciles per the 'do not fabricate' rule rather than estimating a distribution. transport_total = row 7 'Transport' (vehicle purchase + operation + transport services, i.e. total transport spend). transport_work = null: LCF does not publish a work-commute-specific transport split comparable to BLS CES's 'transportation to/from work' subcategory. apparel = row 3 'Clothing & footwear'. communications = row 8 'Communication'. personal_care = row 12.1 'Personal care' (hairdressing, toiletries, cosmetics). education = row 10 'Education' -- SUPPRESSED at decile level (only 'All households'=£5.10/week published); set to null for all deciles, same reasoning as healthcare. childcare = null: LCF/Family Spending has no distinct 'childcare services' COICOP-mapped row comparable to CES; nursery/childminder costs are believed to be embedded within 'Miscellaneous goods & services' or 'Other services' without being separately broken out in the published tables. voluntary_savings = row 14.6 'Savings and investments' -- note this ONS row is explicitly listed under 'Other items recorded' (row 14), which sits OUTSIDE ONS's 'Total expenditure' aggregate (rows 1-13); we still report it here as the schema's best-available proxy for discretionary saving, but it is NOT part of avg_expenditure_total in this file (avg_expenditure_total = ONS's own 'Total expenditure' row, rows 1-13 only, which itself already includes row 13's mortgage-interest/council-tax and money-transfer items but EXCLUDES pension contributions, income tax, National Insurance, and savings -- all reported under row 14 'Other items recorded'). entertainment = row 9 'Recreation & culture'. other = sum of row 5 'Household goods & services' + row 12 'Miscellaneous goods & services' (less its 12.1 personal_care sub-row, already counted separately) + row 2 'Alcoholic drink, tobacco & narcotics' + the residual of row 13 'Other expenditure items' after removing 13.1 (mortgage/council tax, already folded into housing) -- i.e. licences/fines/transfers (13.2), holiday spending (13.3), and money transfers/credit (13.4). This is a residual bucket to absorb categories with no direct v2 schema slot. OTHER CAVEATS: (1) housing_owner_imputed_rent_estimate is null for all deciles -- LCF/Family Spending's 'Housing (net)' concept, unlike BLS CES, is a NET cash-outlay measure for owner-occupiers (structural insurance, minor repairs, water charges, etc.) and does NOT impute a rental-equivalent value for mortgage-free/mortgaged owners the way CES's 'owned dwellings' imputation does; no comparable ONS imputed-rent series by decile was located within the task's step budget. (2) 'avg_expenditure_total' is ONS's own published 'Total expenditure' row (sum of expenditure groups 1-13), not a sum of this file's 'expenditure_by_category' object (which nets out to a slightly different total due to the null suppressions for health/education and the voluntary_savings figure being sourced from outside the official Total-expenditure aggregate) -- consumers of this file should treat avg_expenditure_total as authoritative and the per-category breakdown as best-effort/partially incomplete due to ONS disclosure suppression. (3) housing_owner_share by decile is sourced from a SEPARATE ONS ad-hoc table (FYE 2022 vintage, two years older than the FYE2024 expenditure figures) that cross-tabulates disposable-income decile against four tenure types (owned outright, buying with mortgage, social rented, private rented); owner_share = (owned-outright + buying-with-mortgage households) / (all tenure types), a straightforward share computed from the ad-hoc table's weighted household counts, not modeled or interpolated by us. Values rise monotonically from 44.4% (decile 1) to 82.7% (decile 10), consistent with the well-known UK income-tenure gradient. (4) All 2024 GBP figures are nominal (not adjusted for UK inflation to a different base year); the frontend should apply its own inflation adjustment if comparing against other years' figures. (5) Source numbering in comments (e.g. 'row 1.1') refers to ONS's own COICOP-derived sequential numbering scheme, which the source explicitly notes 'does not use actual COICOP codes' and 'is not comparable to publications before 2001-02'.
